title: What ethics training does NFA require of CFTC registrants?
description: NFA Interpretive Notice 9051 ethics training under Rules 2-9 and 2-36: written procedures, CFTC topics, provider credentials and records, as at November 2026.
shortAnswer: National Futures Association (NFA) Interpretive Notice 9051 treats ethics training as part of every Member's duty to supervise under NFA Compliance Rules 2-9 and 2-36. Members must have written procedures covering topics, providers, format, frequency and documentation, and should address the seven topics in the Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) Statement of Acceptable Practices. Providers need proficiency testing and three years of relevant experience. Firms choose the frequency.
keyTakeaways: Interpretive Notice 9051 (Board of Directors, July 1, 2003; effective September 30, 2019; revised July 21, 2025) states that ethics training is one of a Member's supervisory obligations under Compliance Rules 2-9 and 2-36.
Written procedures must address five things: topics, who provides the training, format, the frequency the Member expects, and how the firm documents that it followed its procedures.
The CFTC Statement of Acceptable Practices in 17 CFR Part 3, Appendix B lists seven topics and acts as a safe harbor for ethics training programs.

Providers, external or in-house, should show completion of relevant proficiency testing and three years of relevant industry experience, and should not be subject to investigations or registration bars.
Section 4p(b) of the Commodity Exchange Act directs the CFTC to require new registrants to attend training within six months of registration and all registrants to attend periodic training.
regulator: National Futures Association (NFA), the self-regulatory organization for the US derivatives industry, under oversight of the Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC)
appliesTo: NFA Member futures commission merchants (FCMs), introducing brokers (IBs), commodity pool operators (CPOs) and commodity trading advisors (CTAs), supervising under Compliance Rule 2-9
Forex Dealer Members, supervising under Compliance Rule 2-36(e)
Associated persons (APs) and principals registered as APs
Personnel of firms relying on registration with another regulator, such as the SEC, to the extent the Commodity Exchange Act applies to their business (per the CFTC Statement)

sections.heading: Where does the NFA ethics training requirement come from?

blocks.text: The requirement rests on three layers: a statute, a CFTC statement and an NFA interpretive notice. Section 4p(b) of the Commodity Exchange Act, [7 U.S.C. 6p](https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/7/6p), directs the CFTC to issue regulations requiring new registrants, within six months after registration, to attend a training session, and all other registrants to attend periodic training sessions, so that registrants understand their responsibilities to the public.

In October 2001 the CFTC replaced its prescriptive ethics training rule with the Statement of Acceptable Practices With Respect to Ethics Training, now at [17 CFR Part 3, Appendix B](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/CFR-2025-title17-vol1/pdf/CFR-2025-title17-vol1-part3-appB.pdf) (66 FR 53521, October 23, 2001). The CFTC describes the Statement as interpretative guidance on fitness and supervision and a "safe harbor" concerning acceptable procedures.

NFA then issued [Interpretive Notice 9051, NFA Compliance Rules 2-9 and 2-36: Ethics Training Requirements](https://www.nfa.futures.org/rulebooksql/rules.aspx?Section=9&RuleID=9051), because Members asked for more detail than the general Statement offered. The notice states that the repeal of the specific CFTC regulations "does not diminish Members' and Associates' obligation to diligently supervise its employees." This page reflects the notice as revised July 21, 2025, and the position as at November 2026.

sections.heading: Why is ethics training treated as a supervision duty?

blocks.text: Because the NFA rules that carry it are supervision rules. [NFA Compliance Rule 2-9(a)](https://www.nfa.futures.org/rulebooksql/rules.aspx?Section=4&RuleID=RULE%202-9) requires each FCM, IB, CPO or CTA Member to diligently supervise its employees and agents in their commodity interest activities, and each Associate with supervisory duties to diligently exercise them. [Compliance Rule 2-36(e)](https://www.nfa.futures.org/rulebooksql/rules.aspx?Section=4&RuleID=RULE%202-36) imposes the same diligent supervision duty on Forex Dealer Members for forex activities.

A practical consequence is that a weak ethics training program is examined and charged as a supervision failure, not as a missed course. NFA staff look at whether the Member's written procedures exist, whether they fit the business, and whether the firm followed them. Rule 2-9 was most recently amended effective March 18, 2026, per the rule's amendment history; the supervision duty in paragraph (a) is unchanged in substance.

sections.heading: What must a Member's written ethics training procedures cover?

blocks.text: Interpretive Notice 9051 says that all firms should have written procedures outlining their ethics training program, and that acceptable procedures will address five matters.

items: The topics that will be included in the training program.
By whom the training will be provided.
The format of the training, for example classroom instruction or software.
The frequency with which the Member expects its employees to obtain ethics training.
How the firm will document that it has followed its written procedures.

blocks.text: These five headings make a usable template for the procedure document itself. The test NFA applies is consistency: the firm should do what its procedures say, and its records should prove it. The [guide to writing a training policy](/guides/how-to-write-a-training-policy) covers the policy structure in more detail.

sections.heading: Which topics should ethics training cover?

blocks.text: Both the CFTC Statement and Interpretive Notice 9051 list seven topics that an ethics training program should address:

items: An explanation of the applicable laws and regulations, and the rules of self-regulatory organizations and contract markets.
The registrant's obligation to the public to observe just and equitable principles of trade.
How to act honestly and fairly and with due skill, care and diligence in the best interests of customers and the integrity of the markets.
How to establish effective supervisory systems and internal controls.
Obtaining and assessing the financial situation and investment experience of customers.
Disclosure of material information to customers.
Avoidance, proper disclosure and handling of conflicts of interest.

blocks.text: The Statement adds that training "should be focused to some extent on a person's registration category," and NFA says Members should tailor programs to their membership category and the roles of their personnel. NFA also notes that, since the Dodd-Frank Act removed the derivatives transaction execution facility category, it is appropriate for training to explain the rules of swap execution facilities that apply to a Member's business.

sections.heading: Who can deliver the training, and how often?

blocks.text: Independent providers, industry associations and in-house trainers are all acceptable, but each must meet the same credential test. Interpretive Notice 9051 says a Member should obtain proof that the provider has completed relevant proficiency testing and has three years of relevant industry experience, or similar experience. NFA may waive the testing requirement where the provider shows comparable competency. Firms should use only providers they reasonably believe in good faith are not subject to investigations or registration bars, and NFA points to its BASIC system for checking registration and disciplinary history.

Format is flexible. The notice names internet, audio, software and video media as well as in-person courses, and permits less formal methods such as distributing periodicals, legal cases and advisories. It also warns that firms with a high percentage of APs with disciplinary histories, or APs from firms with disciplinary histories, may decide that more structured, formal training is appropriate.

Frequency is the Member's decision, based on its business model, the composition of its sales force and the training format. NFA's guidance is that less formal training, such as circulating written materials, should be kept on a more ongoing basis, while formal classroom training could be offered less often but still periodically. Section 4p(b) of the Act frames the baseline: training within six months of registration for new registrants, then periodic training. See [how to set mandatory training refresh cycles](/guides/how-to-set-mandatory-training-refresh-cycles).

NFA calls documentation "a critical element of an acceptable ethics training program." The records depend on the format. Firms that distribute written materials should keep documentation of what was distributed, who selected it, and when and to whom it was circulated. Firms that use formal training should keep records of who obtained the training, the date, and any materials used.

The CFTC Statement adds that evidence of attendance and training materials can be offered to demonstrate fitness and overall compliance during self-regulatory organization audits. For record structure and retention, see [how to prepare training records for an audit](/guides/how-to-prepare-training-records-for-an-audit).

sections.heading: Which other NFA rules require staff training?

blocks.text: Ethics is not the only NFA training duty. Compliance Rule 2-9(c)(4) requires each FCM and IB Member's written anti-money laundering program to provide ongoing training for appropriate personnel, alongside independent testing and a designated AML officer. The US AML picture is covered on the [BSA/AML training requirements](/regulations/bsa-aml-training-requirements) page.

[Interpretive Notice 9070](https://www.nfa.futures.org/rulebooksql/rules.aspx?Section=9&RuleID=9070) on information systems security programs (ISSPs) says a Member's ISSP should describe its ongoing information security training for all appropriate personnel, and that training should be conducted upon hiring and annually during employment, or more often if circumstances warrant. Social engineering is named as a topic to consider.

blocks.text: Members dual registered with the SEC or FINRA should note that Notice 9051 urges them to review the ethics training requirements of the other self-regulatory organizations they belong to. For broker-dealer training duties, see the [FINRA Rule 3110 annual compliance meeting](/regulations/finra-rule-3110-annual-compliance-meeting) page.

sections.heading: How does Knowledge Foundry approach this?

blocks.text: Knowledge Foundry structures ethics training around the seven CFTC topics and the Member's registration categories before content is written, so each module traces to a named topic and audience. Provider credentials, attendance and distribution records attach to that structure, which lets a Member show NFA that it did what its written procedures say. See the [financial services](/industries/financial-services) page.

faqs.q: Does NFA set a minimum number of ethics training hours?
faqs.a: No. Interpretive Notice 9051 leaves frequency to each Member, based on its business model, sales force and training format. The CFTC Statement says firms may require training on whatever periodic basis and duration they and their self-regulatory organizations consider appropriate.

faqs.q: Can a small CTA meet the requirement by circulating articles?
faqs.a: Yes, if its written procedures say so and it documents what was distributed, who selected it, and when and to whom it was circulated. Both the CFTC Statement and Notice 9051 accept distribution of periodicals, legal cases and advisories, and NFA suggests keeping that kind of training on a more ongoing basis.

faqs.q: Can ethics training be delivered in house?
faqs.a: Yes. Notice 9051 states that in-house training is acceptable, but firms should apply the same criteria to in-house trainers as to external providers: relevant proficiency testing, three years of relevant industry experience or similar, and no known investigations or registration bars.

faqs.q: Is the CFTC Statement of Acceptable Practices binding?
faqs.a: The CFTC describes it as interpretative guidance on fitness and supervision that registrants may treat as a safe harbor. The binding duty is supervision under NFA Compliance Rules 2-9 and 2-36, and NFA's Notice 9051 explains how ethics training supports it.

factCheck.claim: Interpretive Notice 9051 is dated Board of Directors July 1, 2003; effective September 30, 2019; revised July 21, 2025, and states that ethics training is one of a Member's supervisory obligations under Compliance Rules 2-9 and 2-36.
Notice 9051 says acceptable written procedures address topics, provider, format, frequency, and how the firm documents that it followed its procedures.

Notice 9051 says Members should obtain proof that providers completed relevant proficiency testing and have three years of relevant industry experience; NFA may waive the testing requirement; in-house trainers face the same criteria.
The CFTC Statement of Acceptable Practices (17 CFR Part 3, Appendix B, 66 FR 53521, October 23, 2001) lists seven ethics training topics and is described as a safe harbor.
7 U.S.C. 6p(b) directs the CFTC to require new registrants to attend a training session within six months after registration and all other registrants to attend periodic training sessions.

NFA Compliance Rule 2-9(a) requires FCM, IB, CPO and CTA Members to diligently supervise employees and agents; Rule 2-9(c)(4) requires FCM and IB AML programs to provide ongoing training for appropriate personnel; amendments effective March 18, 2026 are listed in the rule history.
NFA Compliance Rule 2-36(e)(1) requires each Forex Dealer Member to diligently supervise its employees and agents in their forex activities.
Interpretive Notice 9070 says ISSP training should be conducted upon hiring and annually during employment, or more frequently if circumstances warrant.
